# Linux CPU Scheduling and Local LLM Inference

This project evaluates how `SCHED_OTHER`, `SCHED_BATCH`, and `SCHED_FIFO` affect CPU-only Ollama inference under competing CPU workloads. It implements the supplied research proposal as a reproducible experiment, with raw telemetry, analysis, a four-page report draft, and an eight-slide presentation.

**Status:** the implementation has automated software checks. The repository contains no real model benchmark findings. The report and slides describe the method and the evidence still needed. Files generated by `demo` are visibly labeled synthetic.

## Quick software demonstration on Windows or Linux

Run these commands from the repository root using Python 3.10 or newer:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[analysis]'
python -m scheduler_lab plan --cpus 1-3
python -m scheduler_lab demo --output results/demo
python -m scheduler_lab analyze results/demo --output results/demo-analysis
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

The collector itself has no third-party Python dependencies. Matplotlib and NumPy support plotting. The demonstration assigns no policy benefit in its toy data generator. It exists to verify files and plots, and cannot support a research conclusion.

## Real experiment on Ubuntu 24.04 or WSL2

### 1. Prepare the Linux environment

Open Ubuntu, change to this repository, then run:

```bash
bash scripts/setup_ubuntu.sh
bash scripts/check_environment.sh
```

For this Windows workspace, the Linux path is `/mnt/c/Users/abbas/Desktop/OS/OS-Project`. For more consistent filesystem performance you can copy the repository into your Linux home directory before benchmarking.

Install Ollama using its [official Linux instructions](https://docs.ollama.com/linux). Start the normal Ollama service if it is not already running, then download the explicit quantized model:

```bash
ollama pull llama3.2:3b-instruct-q4_K_M
```

Downloading the weights requires internet access once. Trials use only a local HTTP endpoint. Leave enough RAM for the approximately 3B-parameter model, context, and background processes. Record any swapping in the experiment notes.

### 2. Calibrate and freeze the input

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m scheduler_lab calibrate \
  --model llama3.2:3b-instruct-q4_K_M \
  --threads 3 --output prompts/locked.json
```

This queries the installed model's tokenizer through generation telemetry and adjusts a suffix until Ollama reports exactly 128 prompt tokens with `raw=true`. The lock records the complete text, SHA-256, model digest, quantization details, and server version. The experiment checks the token count and digest again. If your base prompt is already too long or cannot be calibrated, shorten it and retry with a new lock path.

### 3. Select CPUs and the models directory

Use `lscpu -e=CPU,CORE,SOCKET,ONLINE` and `taskset -pc $$` to inspect the available logical CPUs. The default workload set is `1-3`. The harness reserves all remaining allowed CPUs for the normal-priority client, telemetry thread, and watchdog. CPU affinity limits where work can run; it does **not** exclude unrelated host work or isolate physical cores.

Locate the directory containing Ollama's `blobs` and `manifests`. Common locations are `/usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models` for a service install and `$HOME/.ollama/models` for a user install. Pass the actual absolute path. This is essential when the harness runs with `sudo`, which otherwise has a different home directory.

### 4. Run the 35-trial matrix

The FIFO conditions require real-time scheduling permission. The following command runs the controller as root while keeping it under `SCHED_OTHER`. Substitute your actual models path:

```bash
sudo "$(pwd)/.venv/bin/python" -m scheduler_lab matrix \
  --models-dir /usr/share/ollama/.ollama/models \
  --cpus 1-3 --config configs/proposal.json \
  --prompt-lock prompts/locked.json \
  --output results/experiment-01
```

Each trial starts a private loopback Ollama daemon on a fresh port. `taskset` and `chrt` wrap that daemon before it creates its inference runner. The harness samples every descendant's threads to check inherited policy, priority, and affinity. An observed mismatch makes the trial fail. It does not modify the existing Ollama service.

By default, any failed trial stops the matrix with a nonzero exit code. `--keep-going` preserves the failure and continues with the next planned condition. It never silently substitutes a different scheduling policy, removes a successful outlier, or retries until the desired result appears. Use a new output directory for each matrix.

The watchdog deadline defaults to 300 seconds **per complete trial**, including daemon startup and warmup. Increase `--timeout` on slower CPUs. All owned server and stress process groups are terminated on completion, error, or interruption. The preflight check requires enabled RT throttling and a reserved control CPU. The harness does not change kernel scheduling settings. Containers or WSL configurations can still deny FIFO even with root privileges.

With three workload CPUs, 100% contention means three stress workers and 200% means six. The optional full matrix uses two workers for the nominal 50% setting on three CPUs, records its actual 66.7% worker density, and avoids claiming an exact half-core count. Use an even number of workload CPUs if the 50% level is important.

### 5. Analyze and inspect the evidence

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m scheduler_lab analyze results/experiment-01 \
  --output results/experiment-01-analysis
```

The analysis produces `trials.csv`, `summary.csv`, `comparisons.csv`, `analysis.json`, a LaTeX results table, and four figures as 300-dpi PNGs and vector PDFs:

1. `throughput`: mean generation tokens/s and bootstrap 95% intervals.
2. `jitter_cdf`: descriptive pooled inter-token latency distributions at 100% and 200% contention.
3. `context_switches`: sampled involuntary context switches per second, with sample standard deviations.
4. `ttft`: time to first response token versus load, with sample standard deviations.

Use `analysis.json` to check `complete_matrix`, exclusions, and missing trial IDs before writing findings. Trial-level p99 values are the observations for inferential comparisons. With only five pairs, the exact two-sided test has minimum p = 0.0625. More independent replications are needed to resolve p < 0.05 using this test. A 30% effect is a hypothesis to test, never a built-in assumption.

## Report and presentation

The PDF is a four-page, two-column IEEE-style **methodology draft**, not a completed empirical paper. `report/main.tex` provides an IEEEtran source version. `report/build_report.py` builds the shipped PDF from `report/content.json` using ReportLab. LaTeX pagination may differ until you compile it with your chosen IEEEtran installation. Replace the pending-results section after you run and review real experiments, then check the final page count again.

The editable PowerPoint contains eight slides. `presentation/speaker_notes.md` allocates exactly 20 minutes and provides the script, limitations, and discussion prompts. Presenter notes also appear inside the PowerPoint. Update the results slide and conclusion after measured data are available.

See [the method](docs/methodology.md), [data dictionary](docs/data_dictionary.md), [viva questions](docs/viva.md), and [requirements mapping](docs/requirements.md) for details.

## Verification

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
for script in scripts/*.sh; do bash -n "$script"; done
```

Linux tests use an explicitly labeled HTTP test double to exercise real `chrt`, `taskset`, descendant `/proc` telemetry, and watchdog cleanup. These tests do not execute a model. The analysis test is skipped when plotting dependencies are missing. Linux-only checks are skipped on Windows.

## Sources

The implementation uses the official [Ollama generation API](https://docs.ollama.com/api/generate) and [running-model API](https://docs.ollama.com/api/ps). Scheduler details follow the [Linux EEVDF documentation](https://docs.kernel.org/scheduler/sched-eevdf.html), [sched(7)](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/sched.7.html), and [per-thread status fields](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_status.5.html). The bibliography omits proposal references that were not independently verified.
